questions.question: Reaction rate is defined as:
options: The change in the amount or concentration of reactants or products per unit time
The total amount of product formed
The time a reaction takes to finish

questions.question: A flask on a balance loses 3,3 g of CO₂ (M = 44 g·mol⁻¹) in the first 60 s. The average rate over that interval is:
A reaction is fastest:
options: At the start, when reactant concentrations are highest

questions.question: Two runs use identical amounts of reactants, but one runs fifty times faster. Compared with the slow run, the fast run produces:
options: More product per mole of reactant
The same final amount of product — extent is unchanged

subtopics.title: Collision Theory and the Factors That Change Rate

questions.question: For a collision between particles to be effective, the particles must:
options: Collide with correct orientation AND with kinetic energy at least equal to the activation energy
Both be in the gas phase

questions.question: Activation energy is:
options: The energy released by a reaction
The average kinetic energy of the particles
The minimum energy needed for a reaction to occur
The energy stored in a catalyst

questions.question: Fine steel wool ignites in a flame while a solid nail of the same steel only glows, because the wool:
options: Exposes vastly more surface area, so far more particles can collide with oxygen

questions.question: Raising the temperature increases the rate MAINLY because:
options: A much larger fraction of collisions has energy at or above the activation energy

questions.question: In the vanishing-cross experiment, a SHORTER time for the cross to disappear means:
options: A faster reaction — the measurement works as one over time

questions.question: On a volume-time graph, the rate at any moment is read from the:
options: Gradient of the curve at that moment

questions.question: Equal masses of magnesium powder and magnesium ribbon react with the same excess acid. Their volume-time curves will:
options: Start equally steep but end at different plateaus
Start differently — powder steeper — but flatten at the same final volume
Both level off at whatever volume the acid allows

questions.question: If one curve flattens at a LOWER plateau than another, the most reasonable conclusion is that:
options: That run had less reactant available — a different extent

questions.question: On a molecular energy distribution curve, the particles able to react effectively are those:
options: To the right of the activation energy line
At the peak of the curve
To the left of the activation energy line

questions.question: When the temperature is raised, the distribution curve:
options: Grows taller with the same shape
Does not change, but the activation line moves left
Shifts toward higher energies and flattens, with the same total area

questions.question: A catalyst increases the rate by:
options: Providing an alternative pathway with a lower activation energy
Giving every particle more kinetic energy
Increasing the concentration of the reactants

questions.question: On the potential-energy diagram, a catalyst changes:
options: Only the height of the hump — ΔH stays exactly the same

subtopics.title: How Fast Is Not How Far

questions.question: A crushed effervescent tablet in warm water and a whole tablet in cold water release:
options: The same total gas — only the rate differs
More gas from the crushed tablet
More gas from the whole tablet

questions.question: Two gas-volume curves flatten at the same height, but one climbed far more steeply. The steeper one had:
options: A faster rate with the same extent
A greater extent with the same rate

questions.question: Reactions slow down as they proceed because:
options: Reactant particles are used up, so encounters become rarer
The activation energy rises over time

subtopics.title: Bumper Cars That Only Count When They Hit Hard

questions.question: In the bumper-car picture, a 'counting bump' stands for:
options: An effective collision — hard enough and correctly aimed
A collision with the wall of the container

questions.question: Adding more cars to the same floor represents:
options: Increasing the concentration — more collisions per second

questions.question: Grinding a marble lump to powder speeds the reaction because:
options: Powder has a lower activation energy
Particles previously locked inside now sit on exposed surfaces where acid can strike them

questions.question: In the same picture, the catalyst:
options: Pushes every car to a higher speed
Lowers the scoring bar so gentler bumps count, and is never used up
Adds new cars to the floor

subtopics.title: Reading the Story off the Graph

questions.question: On a rate graph, the SPEED of the reaction at any moment is shown by the:
The height of the final plateau records the:
options: Extent — the total amount of product formed

questions.question: Powdered and chunky marble, equal masses, same acid: the powder's curve is steeper. The plateaus will be:
options: At exactly the same height — faster never means more

questions.question: Comparing vanishing-cross runs, a time of 25 s versus 250 s means the 25 s run was:
options: Much faster — think one over time
